<!-- litereview:1f2dd1569b3041d8b1216157b60a3c9a:job:d3ee3b075045436cb439ae34db3816fd:finding:0 -->

#### High · Custom-priced Vertex pass-through deployments are billed at the list price

1. An operator configures a router deployment for a Vertex Gemini model with custom `input_cost_per_token`/`output_cost_per_token`. The router copies those rates into the deployment's `model_info`.
2. A caller sends a non-streamed `:generateContent` request to `/vertex_ai/.../models/<that model>`. `vertex_proxy_route` resolves the deployment, and `_init_kwargs_for_pass_through_endpoint` puts its `model_info` into `metadata`. At that point `use_custom_pricing_for_model` returns `True`.
3. `_create_vertex_response_logging_payload_for_generate_content` prices the response with `litellm.completion_cost(model=..., vertex_location=...)`. That call does not receive custom pricing or the deployment id. This PR now stamps the result into `_hidden_params["response_cost"]`.
4. `Logging._process_hidden_params_and_response_cost` and `response_cost_calculator` return any stamped `response_cost` before they consider `custom_pricing`. The spend row therefore records the cost-map price instead of the deployment's custom rate. Before this PR, the non-streamed path fell through to the calculator and used the custom rate.

The same helper serves the interactions and `rawPredict` handlers, so those paths change the same way. I confirmed the before/after values by calling the handler directly with a local reproducer. I did not run a full proxy.

Smallest fix: skip the stamp when `use_custom_pricing_for_model(logging_obj.litellm_params)` is true. Alternatively, pass `custom_pricing` and `router_model_id` into the helper's `completion_cost` call so the stamped value already honours the deployment rate.

<details>
<summary>Evidence</summary>

Local reproducer `/tmp/repro.py`: a `Logging` object with `litellm_params={"metadata": {"model_info": {"id": "dep-1", "input_cost_per_token": 1e-9, "output_cost_per_token": 1e-9}}}`, `litellm.model_cost["dep-1"]` registered the way the router does it, `gemini-2.5-flash`, 1000 prompt and 1000 completion tokens, `locations/global`.

Head 8278397: `non-stream -> 0.0028`, `model_call_details response_cost: 0.0028` (list price).

Same script with the added `set_hidden_param` line removed (base behaviour): `non-stream -> 2.0000000000000003e-06`, `model_call_details response_cost: 2.0000000000000003e-06` (custom price).

litellm_logging.py `response_cost_calculator`: `if not ignore_stamped_cost and "response_cost" in hidden_params and hidden_params["response_cost"] is not None: ... return hidden_params["response_cost"]` runs before `custom_pricing = self._custom_pricing_for(...)`.

litellm_logging.py `_process_hidden_params_and_response_cost`: `elif "response_cost" in hidden_params: self.model_call_details["response_cost"] = hidden_params["response_cost"]`.

llm_passthrough_endpoints.py `_resolve_vertex_model_from_router` returns `deployment_model_info`, which `vertex_proxy_route` stores on `request.state`. pass_through_endpoints.py then copies it to `_metadata["model_info"]`.

router.py around line 9920 copies `CustomPricingLiteLLMParams` fields into `_model_info` and calls `_register_deployment_in_model_cost(model_id=deployment.model_info.id, ...)`.

The streamed path already showed the list price at base (0.0028) for this setup, so the regression is specific to non-streamed calls.

</details>

[Latest summary by code-review](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/44795#issuecomment-6243362071) · [View this review](https://litereview.onrender.com/runs/1f2dd1569b3041d8b1216157b60a3c9a) · Reviewed `827839794ff4`
Confirmed and fixed in 46f5573409: the stamp now uses deployment custom pricing via completion_cost, with a test covering streamed and non-streamed spend

**Medium: Client metadata can select the billing model**

`init_kwargs_for_pass_through_endpoint()` retains client `metadata.model_info` when no router deployment was resolved, such as Vertex requests using default credentials: an authenticated caller can invoke `gemini-2.5-pro` with `{"metadata":{"model_info":{"id":"gemini-2.5-flash-lite","input_cost_per_token":0}}}` to activate custom pricing and stamp Flash Lite's cheaper registered cost, undercounting spend against their budget. Derive both the custom-pricing flag and deployment ID only from server-resolved deployment data, and ignore client pricing metadata when that data is absent.

pass_through_request strips client metadata.model_info with _strip_client_pricing_overrides before init_kwargs_for_pass_through_endpoint runs, unless the key or team sets allow_client_pricing_override
Thanks for the detail. I can't automatically confirm this is safe to dismiss, so I'm leaving the thread open for a maintainer to make the call.
Superseded by 429e29e10f, which drops the builder's location-blind cost instead of stamping one, so the logger applies the deployment's custom price in both modes

<!-- litereview:12d53544a1234f68909afd16ba6cb1b8:reply -->

**Finding withdrawn**

The reply is correct. At head `429e29e1`, `_create_vertex_response_logging_payload_for_generate_content` only writes the location-aware cost into `kwargs["response_cost"]`. It no longer stamps `_hidden_params`. The streamed path also calls `_drop_location_blind_stream_builder_cost`, which pops the builder's cost. Because no `response_cost` reaches the hidden params, `Logging.response_cost_calculator` skips its stamped-cost early return. It then reaches `_custom_pricing_for` and prices with the deployment's `model_info` rates. This now holds for both streamed and non-streamed calls. The unit tests check the custom price at the logger for both modes, and they fail when the old stamp is put back.

<details>
<summary>Evidence</summary>

`vertex_passthrough_logging_handler.py:790-798` (head): the cost goes only into `kwargs["response_cost"]`. There is no `set_hidden_param` or `_hidden_params` write.

`vertex_passthrough_logging_handler.py:672-681`: `_drop_location_blind_stream_builder_cost` pops `response_cost` from the hidden params of the `stream_chunk_builder` result.

`litellm_logging.py:1945-1956`: the stamped-cost return only fires when `hidden_params["response_cost"]` is present and not `None`, which no longer happens on these paths.

`tests/unit/.../test_vertex_passthrough_logging_handler.py:221-235` and `305-324`: the custom-price tests pass `model_info={"id": deployment, input/output rates}` and assert that the logger records `7*input + 1*output` at the custom rates, for streamed and non-streamed calls.

Run on head: 22 passed. With the stamp temporarily put back after line 797, all 6 `custom_price` cases failed (`comparison failed`). I restored the file afterwards.

`tests/integration/spend/test_vertex_passthrough_regional_uplift_spend.py` also asserts the custom price at the proxy level for finished and cut-off streams. I did not run this proxy test.

</details>

GitHub does not allow this App to resolve this thread. A repository maintainer must do it manually.

Summary

The PR lets the logger price streamed Vertex calls using the endpoint’s region and deployment prices. It also passes the deployment’s location into native Google calls and prices interrupted streams through the logger Since the previous review, non-streamed Gemini calls also leave pricing to the logger. New tests compare streamed and non-streamed Gemini prices, and the earlier test-style finding is fixed - Vertex streams use the logger’s regional and deployment prices. - Interrupted Vertex streams use logger pricing for partial usage. - Google GenAI logging uses the deployment’s Vertex location. - Gemini pass-through calls leave their final price to the logger.
